title: Make pictures, read-aloud and video from a chat

steps.page: Here is how I understand this
steps.intro: What you decided in September, and what I found in the app. Mark each one Holds or Fails.

steps.path: Plan for this work
steps.headline: Pictures come first, then read-aloud, then video.
steps.changed: We build making pictures first. Reading replies aloud comes next, video after that. Searching by meaning stays an idea to explore later, not something we build now.
steps.notice: The first version you try only makes pictures. Read-aloud and video come in later versions.
steps.resolved: All three are now planned together, as you chose; they are still built in that order. Read-aloud, sound and video statements are on their own pages.

steps.path: Any chat
steps.headline: You ask for a picture in an ordinary chat; there is no separate Create screen.
steps.changed: You type something like "make me a poster of…" in a chat. The assistant writes the picture request for you. No new screen, button or menu is added to start it.
steps.notice: Making pictures feels like part of talking to the assistant, not a separate tool.
steps.resolved: Kept in the chat, and the assistant must ask clearly and suggest other ways first (its own statement). The separate studio is filed as an idea for later.

steps.path: A chat where the assistant offers to make a picture
steps.headline: Nothing is made, and nothing is paid, until you press Approve on a card in the chat, except in Full Auto.
steps.changed: Before any picture, sound or video is made, a card appears in the chat showing what will be made, which service makes it and the price. In Full Auto, the permission setting that never asks, the card is skipped and the work starts at once.
steps.notice: In normal chats every item costs one press of yours. In Full Auto things get made without asking; the cost shows afterwards.
steps.caption: Today's closest relative: the card the assistant shows before a step that buys, sends or submits something. The picture card would sit in the same place.
steps.resolved: Added: in Full Auto, the first paid request in a chat goes back to the assistant with your check-in question, and goes ahead only once it has checked with you.

steps.path: The approval card
steps.headline: The card remembers which picture maker you picked last time and starts on it.
steps.changed: The card has a list of picture makers, cheap and pricey, to pick from before you approve. Next time, the list starts on the one you picked last, so you don't choose again each time.
steps.notice: Say you switch to a cheaper maker once. From then on the card starts on that cheaper one until you change it.

steps.path: Any chat
steps.headline: Version one makes new pictures and changes a picture you attach; no painting over one part of a picture.
steps.changed: "Make a picture of…" and "change this picture I attached so that…" both work. Selecting one area of a picture to change only that area is left out.
steps.notice: To change part of a picture you describe the change in words rather than marking the area.

steps.path: The project folder, and the chat's files list
steps.headline: Finished pictures are saved in a pictures folder inside the project and are never deleted automatically.
steps.changed: Each picture is saved as a real file in a scratch pictures folder inside the chat's project. A chat with no project saves to a personal Pictures folder the app keeps. The picture also shows in the chat and in that chat's list of files.
steps.notice: Pictures pile up until you or the assistant move or delete them. The assistant can move a picture to where it belongs.
steps.caption: Today the assistant hands you finished files on a Deliverables card like these. A finished picture would arrive the same way.
steps.resolved: Added as its own statement: every made file carries a label saying it was made by AI and with which model, so you can find and filter them.

steps.path: Settings, where services are connected
steps.headline: For making pictures on your own computer, the app connects to a tool you already run, such as ComfyUI; it installs nothing.
steps.changed: Someone who already runs a picture program on their computer can point the app at it, and it shows up as a choice on the card like any paid service. The app does not download or install a picture engine in this version.
steps.notice: Most people will see only online services on the card. People with their own setup get a free choice that runs on their computer.

steps.path: A chat signed in with a ChatGPT plan
steps.headline: A ChatGPT plan sign-in cannot pay for pictures; a separately paid service is always needed.
steps.changed: OpenAI does not let other apps use a ChatGPT plan to make pictures. Pictures in our app need a separately paid service, such as OpenRouter or an OpenAI key. In a ChatGPT-plan chat the card says so, and says you can make pictures on your plan at chatgpt.com instead.
steps.notice: Someone with only a ChatGPT plan sees two ways forward: connect a paid service here, or use chatgpt.com.

steps.path: Checked in today's code
steps.headline: Today the app can look at pictures and take spoken typing, but it makes no pictures, speech or video.
steps.changed: I searched all of today's app code. You can attach a picture for the assistant to look at, and speak instead of typing. Nothing in the app makes a picture, reads text aloud or makes video.
steps.notice: Everything in this feature is new; there is nothing old to replace or remove.

steps.path: Your own picture of it
steps.headline: If you already picture how any of this looks, describe it here. Skip it if not.
steps.today: Nothing is drawn yet. The next step is two to four drawn designs of the approval card and of a finished picture in the chat.
steps.problem: If you already have a look in mind, drawings that miss it waste a step.
steps.proposal: Anything you write here shapes the first drawings. Leaving it empty is fine.
steps.checked: Nothing has been drawn for this feature as of 2026-11-18.
steps.prompt: For example: the card should look like…, the picture should appear…
steps.resolved: Each idea became its own statement: the right-click Read aloud, the built-in voice, the sound card, pictures shown full size, the picture menu and the video card.

steps.page: Pictures and video in the chat
steps.intro: From your notes: how made pictures and videos show up, and how the assistant decides to make one.

steps.path: Any chat
steps.headline: The assistant offers a paid picture, sound or video only when you clearly ask, and suggests other ways where they fit.
steps.changed: Before reaching for a paid maker, the assistant considers drawing it another way, such as a chart, a simple drawing it writes itself, or a 3D program like Blender, and gives you the pros and cons.
steps.notice: A request like "make a diagram" may get a drawn diagram instead of a paid picture, with a note on why.

steps.path: A finished picture in a chat
steps.headline: A finished picture always shows full size in the chat first, not as a small file card.
steps.changed: The made picture appears in the assistant's reply at full width, as the result. It may also be listed on a files card, but the picture itself always comes first.
steps.notice: You see the picture straight away without opening anything.

steps.path: Right-click any picture in a chat
steps.headline: Right-clicking a picture in the chat opens a menu: copy, save as, open, show in folder.
steps.changed: Every picture in the chat, made or attached, gets a right-click menu with Copy, Save as, Open and Show in folder.
steps.notice: You can paste a picture into another app, or save it somewhere else, in two clicks.

steps.path: Every made picture, sound and video file
steps.headline: Every made file carries a label saying it was made by AI, with which maker and when.
steps.changed: The label is written inside the file itself, so it stays when the file is moved or copied. The app's file lists can show and filter by it.
steps.notice: You can always tell a made picture from a photo, and list only made files.

steps.path: A finished video in a chat
steps.headline: A finished video shows as a card in the chat that opens in your computer's video player; it does not play in the chat.
steps.changed: The card shows the video's first frame, its length and an Open button. Making a video takes minutes; the card shows progress meanwhile, and you can keep chatting.
steps.notice: Video never slows the chat down. Watching it opens your usual video player.

steps.path: The list of video makers on the card
steps.headline: Video is made through OpenRouter or a Google key; OpenAI no longer offers video.
steps.changed: OpenRouter reaches several video makers, including Google's. A Google key reaches Google's directly. OpenAI shut its video service in September 2026.
steps.notice: Video costs more than pictures, often a dollar or more per clip; the card shows the estimate before you approve.

steps.intro: From your notes: reading messages aloud, the voices, and playing sound in the chat.

steps.path: Right-click any message
steps.headline: Right-clicking any message, yours or the assistant's, offers Read aloud.
steps.changed: Read aloud is a new choice in each message's right-click menu. It plays the message in the chosen voice, with a way to stop it.
steps.notice: Any message can be listened to, without asking the assistant.
steps.resolved: Answered in chat: how live voice modes differ from a model plus a voice key, and how the app could build one later.

steps.path: Settings, where the voice is chosen
steps.headline: A pleasant free voice is built into the app; a setting swaps it for a cloud voice paid with your key.
steps.changed: The built-in voice runs on your computer, free and offline. A setting switches to a finer cloud voice, like how naming chats can use the simple way or the assistant.
steps.notice: Read aloud works for everyone at no cost. Better voices are one setting away.

steps.path: The list of cloud voices
steps.headline: Cloud voices use the same services as pictures: OpenRouter, or an OpenAI or Google key you already added.
steps.changed: No new account is needed: the keys already used for pictures also pay for voices.
steps.notice: Google's voices are the cheapest, about a fifth of a cent for ten seconds.

steps.path: A sound in a chat
steps.headline: A sound in the chat shows as a card with play and pause, a simple wave that fills as it plays, and the time.
steps.changed: Any sound the assistant makes, and any recording you send, appears in the chat as this card and plays right there.
steps.notice: You hear sounds in place, without opening another program.

steps.path: The message box
steps.headline: You can send a voice recording as a message, not only speak to type.
steps.changed: Today the microphone turns your speech into typed words. You could also send the recording itself, which appears as a sound card in your message.
steps.notice: Useful for sending a sound for the assistant to work with, like a voice to copy or a clip to tidy up.
steps.resolved: Noted: sending a recording gets its own careful design, including chats whose model cannot hear sound.

steps.intro: Decisions still open. Each has my recommendation; pick one or write your own.

steps.path: The list of picture options on the card
steps.headline: Which paid picture services should the first version work with?
steps.today: The app connects to OpenRouter, OpenAI, Google, Anthropic and a ChatGPT plan, but only to chat with them. None of those connections is used to make pictures.
steps.problem: Each service is one more thing to sign up for and keep working. Too few leaves people without a service they already pay for; too many means more broken options to maintain.
steps.proposal: Start with OpenRouter, where one key reaches about 70 picture makers (OpenAI's, Google's and others). Also use an OpenAI or Google key you have already added.
steps.checked: App code read on 2026-11-18 (the Add provider choices and the provider list). Service details from each company's own pricing and help pages, read 2026-11-18.

options.label: OpenRouter plus keys
options.summary: OpenRouter, plus an OpenAI or Google key you already added.
pros: One OpenRouter key gives the widest choice at the companies' own prices.
People who already added an OpenAI or Google key need no new account.
cons: OpenAI may ask some people to verify their identity before its pictures work.
Google needs billing turned on; its free tier does not cover pictures.

options.label: OpenRouter only
pros: One key, one price list, one thing to set up and keep working.
OpenRouter's list says which makers can edit a picture, so the card can show only suitable ones.
cons: Someone who pays OpenAI or Google directly has to sign up for OpenRouter too.

options.label: Also smaller services
options.summary: Add fal.ai, MuAPI and VideoRouter too.
pros: More choice, and the person who asked on GitHub gets exactly the services they named.
cons: Three more key screens to build and keep working.
MuAPI and VideoRouter are young companies, and neither publishes a list the card can read prices from.

steps.path: Settings, Assistant settings, Cloud providers
steps.headline: Should a key you already added for chatting also pay for pictures?
steps.today: Keys sit on the Cloud providers page, one card per service. Each key is used only for chatting.
steps.problem: If pictures need a separate key, people add the same key twice. If the chat key also pays for pictures, money is spent from a key someone may think of as chat-only.
steps.proposal: The same key covers both. Every picture still waits for your Approve on the card, and the card names the service it will bill.
steps.checked: Cloud providers page checked in today's app code, and photographed, on 2026-11-18.
steps.caption: Today's Cloud providers page. Each card holds one service's key, used only for chatting.

options.label: Same key
options.summary: One key per service, used for chat and pictures.
pros: No extra setup: pictures just work for anyone already connected.
Nothing is spent without your press on the card.
cons: The bill for chats and pictures arrives together from that service.

options.label: Separate picture key
options.summary: Pictures need their own key, even for the same service.
pros: Picture spending is kept apart from chat spending.
cons: Everyone sets up twice.
Two copies of one key to keep up to date.

steps.path: The price shown on the card
steps.headline: What should the card show when the exact price can't be known before the picture is made?
steps.today: Nothing shows a price for pictures, because the app makes none.
steps.problem: Some makers charge a fixed price per picture. Others charge by how much detail they end up drawing, so the exact cost is only known afterwards.
steps.proposal: Show "about $0.04" before, worked out from that maker's price list, then the real cost under the finished picture. If no estimate exists, the card says "price unknown", never "free".
steps.checked: Pricing pages of OpenRouter, OpenAI and Google read 2026-11-18; OpenRouter reports the real cost of each picture once it is made.

options.label: Estimate, then real cost
pros: Every maker can be offered.
You always learn what it really cost.
cons: The real cost can come out a little above the estimate.

options.label: Exact prices only
options.summary: Offer only makers with a fixed price per picture.
pros: What you approve is exactly what you pay.
cons: Leaves out several of the best makers, including OpenAI's newest.

steps.path: Settings, where a picture program on your own computer is connected
steps.headline: Should the first version connect to ComfyUI, a free picture program some people run, or wait for the app's own free engine?
steps.today: Connecting a picture program on your computer, such as ComfyUI, was planned for the first version.
steps.problem: Connecting it is about a week of work, but it keeps breaking as people's setups and models change. Few people run it: it needs a strong graphics card and technical setup.
steps.proposal: Leave it out of the first version. Keep the idea for when the app brings its own free engine that runs on your computer, which serves everyone, not just ComfyUI users.
steps.checked: ComfyUI's own documentation read 2026-11-18. The app's local engine code checked the same day: it runs chat models only.

options.label: Skip for now
options.summary: No local picture option in the first version.
pros: A week sooner, and nothing that breaks with each ComfyUI update.
The later built-in engine helps everyone, not just ComfyUI users.
cons: Pictures cost money until the built-in engine exists.
The few people who already run ComfyUI wait longer.

options.label: Connect ComfyUI
pros: A free choice on the card for people who already run it.
cons: About a week more, plus ongoing fixes as setups change.

steps.path: A chat running Claude Code, and a chat running any other model
steps.headline: Should pictures work in Claude Code chats as well as in chats with the app's other models?
steps.today: The app already gives Claude Code chats some of its own abilities, such as sending you a link or editing Pages. Those work the same in both kinds of chat.
steps.problem: Most people using the app chat through Claude Code. Leaving it out would hide pictures from them; including it means building the card to work in two kinds of chat.
steps.proposal: Both kinds of chat get the same card, the same choices and the same pictures folder.
steps.checked: App code read 2026-11-18: Claude Code chats receive the app's link, Pages, comments and browser abilities.

options.label: Both kinds
options.summary: Same card whatever the chat runs on.
pros: Pictures behave the same everywhere.
Claude Code users can make pictures without changing chats.
cons: A little more to build before the first version is ready.

options.label: Other models first
options.summary: Claude Code chats get it in a later version.
pros: A slightly earlier first version.
cons: Most people would not see the feature at first.

steps.path: Plan for this work
steps.headline: Should read-aloud and video be designed now, or after pictures are built?
steps.today: Nothing is decided yet about how read-aloud or video look or behave.
steps.problem: Designing all three now takes longer before anything ships. Designing pictures alone risks a card that later needs reworking for sound and video.
steps.proposal: Design and build pictures now, keeping the card general enough for sound and video. Read-aloud and video come back as later pages of this same deck.
steps.checked: The September chat closed with the picture plan only; read-aloud and video were listed as still open.

options.label: Pictures first
options.summary: Ship pictures, then design the next one.
pros: You get something to use sooner.
Real use of pictures shapes the read-aloud design.
cons: The card may need small changes when sound arrives.

options.label: Design all three
options.summary: Plan pictures, read-aloud and video together, then build pictures.
pros: One card designed for all three from the start.
cons: Weeks more design before you can make a single picture.

steps.path: The request on GitHub for a picture, sound and video screen
steps.headline: What should we tell the person on GitHub who asked for a picture, sound and video screen and their own keys?
steps.today: A Windows user asked in October for a screen like Open Generative AI, a free picture and video app, and for a place to add MuAPI or VideoRouter keys. Nobody has replied.
steps.problem: They asked for a separate screen, which the first version will not have, and for two services we haven't chosen.
steps.proposal: Thank them, say pictures are coming inside the chat and paid with your own key, and say a separate screen and their two services may come later.
steps.checked: The GitHub request read 2026-11-18: no replies. Open Generative AI's own page shows it makes pictures through MuAPI.

options.label: Reply now
options.summary: Explain the plan and ask if OpenRouter would work for them.
pros: They have waited almost a month; a reply shows the request was heard.
Their answer tells us whether OpenRouter is enough.
cons: It promises a direction before anything is built.

options.label: Reply on release
options.summary: Reply once pictures are in a release.
pros: The reply points at something they can use.
cons: Weeks more silence on a request from a real user.

steps.path: Settings, Permissions, Full Auto
steps.headline: In Full Auto, should an expensive picture, sound or video still stop and ask?
steps.today: Full Auto lets the assistant act without asking. Nothing it does today costs per use.
steps.problem: One video can cost a dollar or more. In Full Auto a misunderstanding, or a loop, could spend real money before you notice.
steps.proposal: Full Auto skips the card for anything under a price you set, one dollar to start. Above it, the card still appears.
steps.checked: Full Auto checked in today's app code on 2026-11-18. Video prices from OpenRouter's and Google's pages, read the same day.

options.label: Ask above a limit
options.summary: Full Auto stops only for items over your limit.
pros: Small items flow without asking.
A mistake can't quietly spend much.
cons: One more setting.
A pricey video still interrupts Full Auto.

options.label: Never ask
options.summary: Full Auto makes everything without the card.
pros: Full Auto never stops.
cons: Nothing caps what a mistake can spend.

steps.resolved: Changed to your plan: each chat starts with a five dollar total for made items; past it, a card offers raising it for that chat in five dollar steps. It survives restarts.

steps.path: The first time you use Read aloud
steps.headline: Should the built-in voice come with the app, or download the first time you use Read aloud?
steps.today: Voice typing works this way: its speech model, about 640 MB, downloads the first time you use the microphone.
steps.problem: A built-in voice adds about 100 MB. Inside the app, everyone downloads it; on first use, the first Read aloud waits for it.
steps.proposal: Download it the first time you press Read aloud, with a progress bar, like voice typing does.
steps.checked: Voice typing download read in today's app code on 2026-11-18. Voice size is typical of small free voices such as Piper and Kokoro.

options.label: On first use
options.summary: Downloads when you first press Read aloud.
pros: The app stays smaller for people who never use it.
Works like voice typing already does.
cons: The first Read aloud waits a minute or so.

options.label: With the app
pros: Read aloud works instantly, even offline from the start.
cons: Every download of the app grows by about 100 MB.
